requirements.quote: The boundary delimiter MUST occur at the beginning of a line, i.e., following a CRLF, and the initial CRLF is considered to be attached to the boundary delimiter line rather than part of the preceding part.
For a body that ends in its close delimiter, multipartPartCount MUST return how many parts the body holds.
The octets before the first delimiter and after the close delimiter MUST be skipped.
Spaces and tabs between a delimiter and its CRLF, RFC 2046's transport padding, MUST be skipped.
A CRLF, two hyphens and the boundary followed by anything but transport padding and a CRLF, or two more hyphens, MUST be read as data.
A part's header field names MUST be matched without regard to case.
A header field other than Content-Disposition and Content-Type MUST be ignored.
Each part MUST contain a Content-Disposition header field [RFC2183] where the disposition type is "form-data".

The Content-Disposition header field MUST also contain an additional parameter of "name"; the value of the "name" parameter is the original field name from the form (possibly encoded; see Section 5.1).
The disposition type MUST be matched without regard to case.
multipartFieldData MUST return the data of the first part whose name is name, octet for octet: every octet from the empty line that ends its header fields to the CRLF of the delimiter after it.
multipartFieldData and multipartFieldFilename MUST return null when no part before the close delimiter has that name, and when the body is refused before one does.

multipartFieldFilename MUST return the filename parameter of the first part whose name is name as the sender wrote it, quotes removed: a backslash inside the quotes is an octet like any other, so a Windows path such as C:\x.txt keeps its backslash, and a browser's escaped quote %22a%22.txt stays as given.
multipartFieldFilename MUST return null for a part with no filename parameter.
A filename* parameter MUST NOT be read in place of filename.
multipartPartCount MUST return -1 for a boundary that is empty, longer than 70 octets, holds an octet outside RFC 2046's bchars or ends in a space.
multipartPartCount MUST return -2 for a body with no opening delimiter, or whose part's header lines or data run to its end.
multipartPartCount MUST return -3 for a header line that ends in a CR or LF alone, starts with a space or tab, or has no colon, and for a part with two Content-Type fields.
multipartPartCount MUST return -4 for a part with more than 16 header lines, or more than 8192 octets of them.
multipartPartCount MUST return -5 for a part with no Content-Disposition, two of them, one whose type is not form-data, or one with no name parameter.
multipartPartCount MUST return -6 for a body of more than 64 parts.

clauses.title: a field and a file, as a browser sends them
a preamble, padding, a boundary mid-line and an epilogue
the second part's data
the CRLF before a delimiter is the delimiter's, the one before it the data's
a longer boundary after a CRLF and two hyphens is data
the data of a one-part body is what was sent, whatever its octets
two parts are counted, and the second is found by its name
a preamble and an epilogue of any octets are skipped
any run of spaces and tabs after a delimiter is transport padding
a longer boundary after a CRLF and two hyphens is data
a part is found by the name it was sent under, and by no other
a field name and a disposition type in another case are read
a header field of any other name is ignored
a name no part has, and a body refused before its part, give null
a file name is returned as written, backslashes and percent signs kept
a part with no filename parameter has none, even with filename*
a boundary of 1 to 70 bchars frames, and one of 71 or more is -1
an empty boundary, one with a semicolon and one ending in a space are -1
no opening delimiter, data to the end and header lines to the end are -2
a line with no colon, a folded line, a bare LF and a second Content-Type are -3
17 header lines, or a line past 8192 octets of them, are -4
